masteryZone.q: Which CPU unit performs logical comparisons?
masteryZone.sol: ALU performs all arithmetic calculations and logical comparisons.

masteryZone.q: What is the second step of the instruction cycle?
masteryZone.sol: Decode is the second step, where the instruction in the IR is interpreted.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Registers reside outside the CPU chip on the motherboard.
masteryZone.sol: False. Registers are located directly inside the CPU core for speed.

masteryZone.q: What is the third stage of the machine cycle?
Which register holds the current instruction being executed?
masteryZone.sol: Instruction Register (IR) holds the current instruction binary code.

masteryZone.q: Which register holds ALU intermediate calculation results?
masteryZone.sol: Accumulator holds intermediate arithmetic and logical results.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Program Counter (PC) holds the address of the current instruction being executed.
masteryZone.sol: False. PC holds the address of the NEXT instruction to be executed.

masteryZone.q: Which register connects directly to the Address Bus?

masteryZone.sol: Address Bus is strictly unidirectional, carrying targets from CPU to RAM/IO.

masteryZone.q: Which architecture separates instruction and data memories/buses?
masteryZone.sol: Harvard architecture uses physically separate paths and storage for code and data.

masteryZone.q: True or False: RISC architectures execute simple instructions in single clock cycles.
masteryZone.sol: True. RISC instructions are simplified to complete in a single cycle using pipelining.
